title: Keep the humans.txt timeout active through body reading
prompt:
Ensure the humans.txt validator's eight-second timeout covers the response body. Evidence: src/app/api/validate-humans-txt/route.ts:10-19 creates an abort deadline for fetch, line 21 clears it immediately after headers arrive, and line 30 then awaits res.text() without a deadline. A local execution with instrumented timers confirmed that body reading starts after the timeout has been cancelled. An upstream server that sends headers promptly but stalls its body can therefore leave the user waiting indefinitely.

Change only src/app/api/validate-humans-txt/route.ts in production. Keep the abort timer active until the entire fetch and body-read operation finishes, and clear it in a finally block on every success or failure path. Ensure an aborted body read reaches the existing fetch-failure response. Preserve the current HTTP-status propagation, invalid-JSON 422 response, and successful JSON behavior. Do not change the frontend classification already delivered by merged PR #21 or expand this into URL-policy work.

Add tests/humans-validator-body-timeout.test.mjs using mocked fetch and controlled timers with an abort-aware body promise. Test immediate headers followed by a stalled body, successful body completion before the deadline, fetch rejection, non-OK upstream response, and invalid JSON; assert timers are cleaned up. Run node --test tests/humans-validator-body-timeout.test.mjs tests/humans-validator-errors.test.mjs. Use no real network requests. work on the assigned branch you are on. No credentials, deploys, sends, payments, migrations, workflow, package.json, or auth changes.
